steps.note: Start the RFQ event setup required for the pending counter-offer scenario.
Provide the mandatory event title.
Use an RFQ pricing stage, which supports counter offers.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding items.
Add a line item for the RFQ quote.
Complete the pricing sheet so the event can be published.
Commit a valid bidding schedule.
Invite the QA vendor who will submit and modify the bid.
Publish the RFQ so the vendor can bid.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Confirm the vendor’s original bid was accepted.
Open the buyer comparison grid to send a counter offer.
Send a pending counter offer to the bidding vendor.
Confirm the buyer grid marks the counter offer as initiated.
Continue as the vendor persona in the supplier portal.
Open the event overview where the pending counter offer response is available.
Open the vendor’s counter-offer response choices by selecting Decline.
Choose the modification path requested by the case.
Assert that an editable value field is exposed for the modified bid.
Assert that the blue Place Modified Bid action is available.
